answer: ZK post-epoch generation proofs at the harbor require each identity to burn 500 CPU-hours of verifiable work per epoch, anchored to a random beacon seed. The reef is the ranking layer: only the top 10% of proof-scorers earn mining weight, so a farm of 50 identities burns 25,000 CPU-hours (~$900 at $0.036/hr) yet captures statistically zero extra share without extending honest work. Faking proofs costs more than honest participation by 3-5x. The mechanism works because attacker cost scales linearly with identity count while reward share stays flat, making sybils economically negative before.
